regions.title: Tahoe
regions.text: Kirkwood leads with 26" over the window, and the big day is Wednesday with 21". The NWS is calling for more, 47" Sunday night through Wednesday night. A Winter Storm Warning runs Friday through Saturday. Sugar Bowl and Palisades are close behind, each near 24".

regions.title: Eastern Sierra
regions.text: Mammoth expects 13" through Wednesday, with the best snow Wednesday at 11". The NWS is calling for more, 20" Sunday night through Wednesday night. Gusts to 60 mph Wednesday night will make the upper lifts tough. A Winter Storm Warning runs Friday through Saturday.

regions.title: Coast Mountains
regions.text: Whistler looks mostly wet this week, with rain Saturday night and Sunday and a 7" day Saturday that falls mostly as rain at valley levels. Expect 13" total. Cypress Mountain is milder and windier, with 3" total and southeast gusts up to 70 km/h near the water.

regions.title: Cascades
regions.text: Crystal Mountain leads at 6" total, with its best day Sunday at 3". Snow levels stay low, so expect rain mixed in through the weekend and cold snow later. Stevens Pass is close at 6", and Mt. Baker has 5" spread evenly across Saturday through Monday.

regions.title: Northern Rockies
regions.text: Big Sky should get 8", with the bulk Tuesday at 7". The NWS is calling for more, 14" Monday night through Wednesday. Sun Valley adds 4" and Grand Targhee 3", both mostly Monday through Wednesday.

regions.title: Central Rockies
regions.text: Telluride gets 7" over the window, with 4" on Saturday. The NWS is calling for more, 14" through Wednesday. Crested Butte is at 3", with the main snow Wednesday, and the NWS is calling for 8" through Wednesday. Steamboat adds 2" Tuesday.

regions.title: Southern Rockies
regions.text: Wolf Creek has 7" over the window, and the NWS is calling for more, 27" Saturday through Wednesday. Expect gusts to 60 mph Tuesday night. A Winter Weather Advisory covers Saturday into Saturday night. Taos is at 3", with the NWS calling for up to 11" through Tuesday night.

ahead.text: The Weather Prediction Center says another Pacific storm may bring heavy Sierra snow around Friday Nov 20. It has low confidence in the exact track.
